A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EyeMulator study, with matching authors, framework, benchmarks and principal results. Text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. V1 has no appendix; v2's Appendices A-C are readable and included.

before.justification: V1 reports original CodeXGlue model evaluations, gaze-data analyses, reading-versus-writing comparisons, component ablations and attention measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original model evaluations and attention analyses and adds generated-output case studies in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The framework remains, but the reported optimization changes substantially. V1 Section 3.4 samples two candidate outputs for DPO; v2 Section 2.4 instead compares a pseudo-scan path with its complement. Mask quotas also change from normalized fixation counts to posterior salience. Algorithm 1 additionally restricts SFT to path positions, although this conflicts with v2's unrestricted prose formula. These are changes to the described procedure, not proof of corresponding implementation changes.

E1.justification: Both use EyeTrans gaze data and CodeXGlue Java completion, Java-to-C# translation and Java-to-English summarization. Appendix C's new examples remain within these tasks. Other languages and interactive development environments remain proposed future work.

E2.justification: The reported principal comparisons retain StarCoder, Llama-3.2 and DeepSeek-Coder. V2 Section 3 newly names Random Attention as a comparator, but no results table, findings passage or appendix identifies its outcome. Its actual participation in the evaluation cannot be established.

E3.justification: The stated translation split changes from 8,701/431/836 training/validation/test examples in v1 Section 4.2 to 10,300 training and 500 test examples in v2 Section 3. This substantially changes the reported evaluation setting despite identical Table 2 scores; rerunning is not established. Metric documentation also differs: v1 specifies BERTScore F1, whereas v2 Appendix A supplies a one-sided matching formula without explaining the change.

E4.justification: V2 reduces Table 3 from fifteen task subcategories to five, removes summarization component-ablation results, and omits all translation attention-metric results. Appendix C adds two case studies concerning malformed translation output and repetitive summaries. These substantially revise the supporting analyses; the existing gaze plots and attention maps remain.

E5.justification: V1 specifies random seed 42 and reports p-values for twelve attention-metric comparisons in Table 5. V2 removes the seed disclosure and all these significance values, including for retained comparisons. No repeated-run variability or confidence intervals replace them.

E6.justification: All sixty principal scores in Table 2 remain identical, but numerous gaze-count, subgroup, ablation and attention-result entries disappear, and Appendix C adds two output comparisons. Summarization baseline entropy changes from 23.79 in v1 Table 5 to 88.2 in v2 Table 4, reversing the tabulated direction against EyeMulator's 60.41/60.4. V1 already contained conflicting prose using 88.21; v2 does not explain the replacement.

T1.justification: Formal specifications change locally: Algorithm 1 sums SFT over pseudo-path positions instead of v1's target-masked sequence, and the quota basis changes from fixation proportions to posterior means. Appendix A's BERTScore expression also differs from v1's stated F1 definition. Most other metric mathematics is retained or restated; neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains architecture-independent gaze-informed fine-tuning with improvements across three tasks. V2 strengthens the introductory premise by asserting that existing models distribute attention uniformly and fundamentally lack logical-dependency prioritization. It also explicitly attributes gains to attention alignment rather than mere overfitting, without adding a reported control establishing that distinction.

C2.justification: V2 corrects v1's assertion that combined priors win every subgroup, acknowledging that specialized reading or writing priors often perform best. It adds failure-mode interpretations and explicit limits on interactive-environment and demographic generalization. Conversely, it removes v1's construct-validity warning that fixation does not establish cognitive importance, along with detailed qualifications about gaze noise and algorithmic approximations.

D1.justification: V2 Section 3 and Appendix B newly disclose full-parameter tuning, AdamW, learning rate, batch size, sequence length, epochs, precision and loss hyperparameters, and provide public artifact-access information. These are primarily disclosures rather than established setting changes. However, v1's exact completion/summarization split sizes, gaze dispersion threshold and mode-specific line-span settings are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds works including Vaswani et al. (2017), Li et al. (2024) on human/model code attention, and Fang et al. (2025) on DPO-F+. It removes several background references, including the CodeBLEU and CrystalBLEU papers. The central positioning against architecture-specific gaze approaches such as EyeTrans remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation, results discussion and related work are extensively rewritten and condensed. The separate Preliminaries section disappears, metrics move into Appendix A, and subword projection is folded into other sections. Limitations move after the conclusion, while ethics, data availability and three appendices are added.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different document layout, typography and author block. Existing Figures 1-7 are repositioned and recaptioned; Tables 1 and 3 are shortened, and portions of v1 Tables 4-5 are merged into a compact two-panel Table 4. Algorithm 1, a hyperparameter table and case-study Figures 8-9 are added.

improvement.justification: V2 improves implementation disclosure and artifact-access information and corrects the session-mode interpretation. However, it removes substantial supporting analyses and significance reporting while changing the stated translation split and training specification without reconciling unchanged benchmark scores. The unexplained entropy replacement adds uncertainty. These benefits and unresolved empirical inconsistencies prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
